analysis.title: US Economic Weekly: Fed call change: Adding a hike in Jan '27
key_insights: BofA added a 25bp Fed hike in Jan '27. It now expects hikes at the next three meetings (Dec, Jan, Mar), for a terminal rate of 4.5-4.75%.

After Oct CPI the Fed looks further behind the curve on inflation and no longer has the luxury of hiking at a quarterly pace. BofA thinks most of the FOMC has or will come around to the view that the October pause was a mistake.

The new call came after a hot, broad-based core CPI in October and a very strong October jobs report. BofA sees the whole distribution of Fed outcomes as having moved to the right, so it prefers a base case of three more hikes with balanced risks over two hikes with upside risks.
Markets are pricing over 45bp of cumulative hikes by the Jan meeting. BofA says a Dec hike looks like a done deal.
Gov. Waller said the Fed needs to at least take back the 75bp of risk-management cuts from last year. BofA expects the Fed to reverse all of the 2025 cuts and one from 2024.

Downside risks to the call: a soft patch in inflation or jobs data, a US-Iran deal that sustainably lowers oil prices, or a significant equity selloff. BofA calls this a reflexively dovish committee that could delay the last hike to Apr or Jun, or skip it.

Upside risks: a labor market that tightens and drives a wage inflation surge, or another year of very large annual price resets in 1Q '27, which could push the policy rate above 5%. The base case is smaller resets than last year, as diesel is well off the highs, though AI-related input costs keep rising.

BofA does not expect a 50bp hike in Dec, for five reasons: it would be a big shift from quarterly hikes, oil has dropped sharply, the optics would make the Oct pause look political, tepid wage inflation (unit labor costs -/+2.4% y/y) gives doves an argument, and a 50bp move could unanchor policy pricing given Chair Warsh's unwillingness to guide markets.
A 50bp Dec hike would need most or all of: Oct core PCE near 40bp, a 4.0% Nov u-rate, 0.4% Nov wage inflation, doves on board, and market pricing of at least a 50% chance of 50bp.
BofA has no cuts penciled in for '27 or '28 but sees a slightly higher probability of cuts in 2H '27 or '28 given the higher terminal rate.

Oct CPI topped expectations for a third consecutive month: headline +0.4% m/m and core +0.3% m/m versus 0.3% and 0.2% consensus. BofA raised its Oct core PCE tracking from 0.23% to 0.32% m/m (3.3% y/y).

Oct retail sales preview: BAC card spending per household rose just 0.1% m/m in Oct, but online retail rebounded and seasonal factors should help. BofA forecasts ex-auto and control group sales both +0.4% m/m, and headline +0.2%.

Oct FOMC minutes preview (Wed 11/18, 2pm): BofA expects a deeper divide over the hold than the 10-2 vote suggested. Those favoring the hold argued higher yields were doing some of the Fed's work. Those opposed stressed economic strength and the risk of falling behind, and the latter camp is likely to push for a faster pace of hikes.
3Q GDP tracking is 3.9% q/q saar, up 0.1pp, versus 3.4% for the advance print. BofA's growth forecast is 2.6% 4Q/4Q for 2026 and 2.1% for 2027.
BofA expects core PCE to finish 2026 above 3%, declining to 2.5% in 2027. Inflation risks are skewed to the upside, with tariffs, energy and increasingly AI cited as drivers.
Labor forecast: job growth of 85k/mo in '26 and about 60k in '27 and '28, with the u-rate at 4.1% through 2027.

Fed speakers have mostly voiced hawkish concern: Logan wants at least two more 25bp hikes, Daly expects further tightening, Waller floated 50bp in Dec, Williams called inflation far too high, and Goolsbee called the CPI 'borderline disturbing'. Hammack and Barkin favor smaller, gradual steps.
Card spending per household slowed to 5.1% y/y in the week ending Nov 7, likely because gas price inflation moderated, but remains resilient.

macro_indicators.interpretation: BofA expects 25bp hikes in Dec '26, Jan '27 and Mar '27 from the current 3.75-4.00% range, with the final hike possibly delayed or skipped.
Markets are already pricing roughly two 25bp hikes by January, in line with BofA's new call.
Above the 0.3% consensus, the third straight upside surprise.
Above the 0.2% consensus, with broad-based price gains led by core goods.
Revised up from 0.23% after the CPI data. A reading near 0.40% would support a 50bp hike case.
The advance GDP print was 3.4%, so tracking points to stronger growth.
BofA expects a trend-like report despite weak card data.
Feeds into the Oct PCE estimate.
Unit labor costs declined outright in 3Q, which gives doves a reason to oppose a 50bp hike.
Slightly above expectations but low in absolute terms.
Below consensus and below the prior 3.97M.

risk_factors: Wage inflation surge or large 1Q '27 annual price resets could push the policy rate above 5%.
A soft patch in inflation or jobs data, a sustained oil price drop from a US-Iran deal, or a significant equity selloff could delay or skip the final hike.
Tightening financial conditions, which were one reason the Fed held in October.
AI-related input costs and AI data center demand continue to add to inflation.
The higher the terminal rate, the greater the risk that something in the economy breaks.
vol_and_positioning: Fed funds futures price over 45bp of cumulative hikes by the Jan meeting and nearly 50bp over the next two meetings.
BofA notes Chair Warsh's unwillingness to guide markets raises the risk that a 50bp hike could unanchor policy pricing and tighten financial conditions unduly.
geopolitical: A US-Iran deal leading to a sustained drop in oil prices is cited as a downside risk to the hike path.
Musalem cites negative supply shocks related to the Middle East as a source of excess inflation.

tension_points.bull_case: Hawkish case: inflation is broad based, the labor market is strong, and the Fed is behind the curve, so a Jan '27 hike is added and the policy rate could go above 5% if wages surge or price resets are large.
tension_points.bear_case: Dovish case: this is a reflexively dovish committee, and a soft patch in data, a US-Iran deal lowering oil, or an equity selloff could delay or skip the last hike.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A soft patch in inflation or jobs data over the next four months of releases before the March meeting, a sustained oil price drop from a US-Iran deal, or a significant equity selloff.

tension_points.bull_case: Waller opened the door to 50bp in Dec if core CPI came in around 0.3% or higher, which it did.
tension_points.bear_case: Quarterly-pace habits, lower oil, political optics, tepid unit labor costs, and the risk of unanchoring policy pricing argue against it.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A 50bp hike would become likely with Oct core PCE near 40bp, a 4.0% Nov u-rate, 0.4% Nov wage inflation, doves on board, and at least a 50% market chance of 50bp.
